correctness.rationale: From the actual p-convex free-lattice functional norm over dual rows v_r, the ℓ1 base unit ball implies the weak-p row constraint max_j Σ_r |v_{rj}|^p<=1. With M=max_{||u||p=1}|f(u)|, homogeneity gives Σ|f(v_r)|^p<=M^p Σ_j Σ_r |v_{rj}|^p<=nM^p. For any unit u, the orbit rows v_g=(n/|G|)^{1/p}gu have EXACTLY unit column p-energy by transitivity, and invariant f has Σ_g|f(v_g)|^p=n|f(u)|^p. Thus exact norm n^(1/p)M; for p=∞ the free AM norm is sup. Finite-dimensional free lattice represents all continuous positively homogeneous functions on the dual sphere; scaling and quotient invariance give onto C(S_p/G). Averaging G gives norm-one positive projection but not lattice-homomorphic averaging. Disjoint h=(|u1|-|u2|)+ and k reversed each norm1 while h∨k has norm 2^(1/p)>1 for finite p. Rearrangement s_k has norm (n/k)^(1/p). Independently rechecked orbit column identity for n=4, p=2 and inspected original verify_orbit.py. No finite example proves all dimensions, which follow from the analytic orbit identity.

originality.rationale: Checked primary free p-convex lattice norm and finite-dimensional homogeneous function-space results. Jardón-Sánchez–Laustsen–Taylor–Tradacete–Troitsky prove the general free p-convex norm functional model; Laustsen–Tradacete identify underlying finite-dimensional continuous-function lattices, but they do not establish a transitive-coordinate fixed-point ISOMETRIC norm equality n^(1/p) max or its norm-one complemented AM sublattice. The orbit-saturation proof is genuinely additional. Resultary semantic aliases for transitive permutation invariants, cyclic orbit averages, fixed-point AM-space and exact multiplier returned the assigned research statement and unrelated lattice invariants, not a distinct prior theorem. Best-of-knowledge acceptance records unindexed invariant-subspace possibility rather than treating failed searches as a novelty proof.
residual_risks: Other less-indexed papers or theses on permutation-invariant free lattices could state the exact fixed-point formula; priority is best of knowledge.
Analysis is real scalar and coordinate-permutation actions on ℓ1^n; nontransitive actions need not satisfy the same n^(1/p) formula.
Averaging projection is positive and norm one, NOT in general a lattice homomorphism; retain distinction.

value.rationale: Every transitive subgroup (including a small cyclic subgroup) produces an explicit norm-one-complemented AM-space inside a free p-convex lattice that itself violates the disjoint-supremum AM identity, with exact renorming constant and quotient representation. This is structural information about free Banach lattices and symmetry, not just routine substitution in a scalar norm; the contrast and sharp orbit witness give mathematical motivation independent of reproducibility.

final_claim: For n>=2, 1<=p<=infinity and any transitive coordinate subgroup G<=S_n, the invariant sublattice FBL^(p)[ℓ1^n(R)]^G is isometrically lattice isomorphic to C(S_p/G), via f↦n^(1/p) f|_{S_p}; it is norm-one complemented and, for finite p, an AM-space within non-AM ambient free lattice.
limitations: Real n>=2; 1<=p<=∞, arbitrary finite transitive G<=S_n, no arbitrary group or base-space extension.
No independent formal proof assistant or outside expert attestation is claimed.
